\begin{remark}[Circular gates]
Two bugs passed the experiment's consistency gate, because the gate's predicted yield shared their omission: missing prime-power lines, and a modular inverse computed once instead of once per root. Both were caught only by an independent brute-force recount. A third issue, mixed logarithm bases inflating $u$, was caught in a smoke test. A gate whose prediction shares the implementation's assumptions cannot falsify them.
\end{remark}

\section{From relations to a factor}

\begin{proposition}[Congruence of squares]\label{prop:congr}
For any finite family $(x_i)_{i\in T}$, $N\mid\bigl(\prod x_i\bigr)^2-\prod(x_i^2-N)$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Induction, using $(x_jX)^2-(x_j^2-N)P=x_j^2(X^2-P)+NP$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Square dependency]\label{prop:dep}
If $x_1,\dots,x_n$ give positive $B$-smooth values $x_i^2-N$ and $n>|\mathcal P(N,B)|$, there is a nonempty $T$ and $Y\in\Z$ with $\prod_{i\in T}(x_i^2-N)=Y^2$, and hence $N\mid(\prod_T x_i)^2-Y^2$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
The exponent-parity vectors lie in $\F_2^{\mathcal P(N,B)}$ by Proposition~\ref{prop:support}. More vectors than the dimension are dependent. Then apply Proposition~\ref{prop:congr}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Factor extraction]\label{prop:gcd}
If $N\mid X^2-Y^2$, $N\nmid X-Y$ and $N\nmid X+Y$, then $1<\gcd(X-Y,N)<|N|$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
If the gcd were $1$, then $N\mid X+Y$. If it were $|N|$, then $N\mid X-Y$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[End-to-end]
If $\prod_{i\in T}(x_i^2-N)=Y^2$ and $\prod x_i\not\equiv\pm Y\pmod N$, then $\gcd(\prod x_i-Y,N)$ is a proper divisor of $N$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Four roots, two useful]\label{thm:crt}
Let $p\neq q$ be odd primes and $y$ a unit modulo $pq$. Then $x^2\equiv y^2\pmod{pq}$ has exactly $4$ solutions, exactly $2$ of which satisfy $x\not\equiv\pm y$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
By the Chinese Remainder Theorem the solutions correspond to $\{\pm y_p\}\times\{\pm y_q\}\subset\F_p\times\F_q$, which has four elements because $b\neq-b$ for $b\neq0$ in odd characteristic. Removing $\pm y$ leaves $(y_p,-y_q)$ and $(-y_p,y_q)$.
\end{proof}

\subsection*{A certificate for $N=103\,764\,863$}
With factor base $\{2,11,17,19,23,31,37,43,47,59\}$, elimination over $\F_2$ produced, among others, the following two dependencies. The first, $x\in\{10342,10749,18185\}$, has value product $92\,360\,250\,334^2$ and $N\mid 10342\cdot10749\cdot18185-92\,360\,250\,334$, so it is \emph{trivial}. The second is
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}rrl@{}}\toprule
$x$ & $x^2-N$ & factorization\\\midrule
$10248$ & $1\,256\,641$ & $19^2\cdot59^2$\\
$10342$ & $3\,192\,101$ & $11^2\cdot23\cdot31\cdot37$\\
$10749$ & $11\,776\,138$ & $2\cdot11\cdot17\cdot23\cdot37^2$\\
$18185$ & $226\,929\,362$ & $2\cdot11\cdot17\cdot23^2\cdot31\cdot37$\\\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
Its product is $Y^2$ with $Y=103\,535\,840\,624\,414$. With $X=\prod x_i=20\,716\,911\,864\,941\,040$, the dependency is non-trivial and $\gcd(X-Y,N)=9127$, so $N=9127\times11369$ with both factors prime. \begin{remark}[A Fermat shadow]
The first relation is itself a square: $10248^2-N=1121^2$, so $N=(10248-1121)(10248+1121)=9127\times11369$, which is Fermat's method inside the sieve. It occurs because the factors are close, so $(p+q)/2$ lies only about $62$ above $\sqrt N$.
\end{remark}
Every relation here is non-squarefree. By Corollary~\ref{cor:first}, a first-power sieve with an exact threshold would have rejected all four.

\section{Algorithms}

\begin{algorithm}[Hensel line generation]
For an odd prime $p\nmid N$: if $\leg Np=-1$, return no lines. Otherwise find $r^2\equiv N\pmod p$ and, for each level and each root separately, set $x\leftarrow x-(x^2-N)(2x)^{-1}\bmod p^{k+1}$. Cost: $O(K)$ inversions per prime.
\end{algorithm}

\begin{algorithm}[Exact-threshold log sieve]
For each admissible $p$, level $k\le K$ with $K\ge\log_2\max Q$, and root $r$, add $\log p$ at $x\equiv r\pmod{p^k}$. Keep $x$ if the accumulator is at least $\log Q(x)-\varepsilon$, and trial-divide survivors only. Cost: Theorem~\ref{thm:work}.
\end{algorithm}

\begin{algorithm}[Dependency search and extraction]
Run Gaussian elimination on parity vectors over $\F_2$. For each dependency compute $X$, $Y$ modulo $N$ and test $\gcd(X-Y,N)$. Cost: $O(|\mathcal P|^2n)$ bit operations.
\end{algorithm}

\section{Discussion}
The sieve is a filter, and its input is a restricted population. Its speed-up over trial division is the constant ratio of $\pi(B)$ divisions to a few additions per value, and the filter is exact once prime powers are sieved. The yield is not that of random integers. The support is the admissible half of the primes (Proposition~\ref{prop:support}), each hit along two lines at every level (Theorem~\ref{thm:lines}). The effective-$u$ heuristic captures the first effect and not the second, which is why it gets the direction right but overshoots the size. The asymptotic QR-restricted yield law is not proved here. Only the algebraic identity behind the shift is.

\section{Future work}

\begin{conjecture}[QR-restricted Dickman law]
For non-square $N$ and $u\in[3,4]$, the proportion of $x\in[\sqrt N,\sqrt N+M]$ with $x^2-N$ $B$-smooth is asymptotic to $\rho_{1/2}(u)$, where $u\rho_{1/2}'(u)=-\tfrac12\rho_{1/2}(u-1)$, up to a local Euler-product correction.
\end{conjecture}

\begin{conjecture}[Prime-power share law]
The fraction of smooth values $x^2-N$ that are not squarefree converges, for fixed $u$, to an explicit $c(u)\in(0,1)$ given by an Euler product over admissible primes with local densities $2/p^2$. The exact-threshold loss decreases monotonically in $B$.
\end{conjecture}

Further directions include direct measurement of $x^2-N$ smoothness against a QR-restricted reference pool at $u\in[3,4]$, and testing the $2^{-d}$ failure law of Theorem~\ref{thm:crt} over many semiprimes.

from __future__ import annotations

# Elementary number theory
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
def primes_up_to(n: int) -> List[int]:
    """Sieve of Eratosthenes."""
    if n < 2:
        return []
    is_p = bytearray([1]) * (n + 1)
    is_p[0] = is_p[1] = 0
    for i in range(2, math.isqrt(n) + 1):
        if is_p[i]:
            is_p[i * i :: i] = bytearray(len(is_p[i * i :: i]))
    return [i for i in range(n + 1) if is_p[i]]


def legendre(a: int, p: int) -> int:
    """Legendre symbol (a | p) for an odd prime p, via Euler's criterion."""
    t = pow(a % p, (p - 1) // 2, p)
    return -1 if t == p - 1 else t


def sqrt_mod_prime(a: int, p: int) -> Optional[int]:
    """A square root of a modulo the odd prime p (brute force; p is small)."""
    a %= p
    for x in range(p):
        if x * x % p == a:
            return x
    return None


def hensel_roots(N: int, p: int, k: int) -> List[int]:
    """All roots of x^2 = N (mod p^k), p odd, p not dividing N.
    Lifts each root mod p step by step: y = x - (x^2 - N) * (2x)^{-1} mod p^{j+1}."""
    r = sqrt_mod_prime(N, p)
    if r is None:
        return []
    roots = sorted({r, (-r) % p})
    mod = p
    for _ in range(1, k):
        new_mod = mod * p
        lifted = []
        for x in roots:
            inv = pow(2 * x, -1, new_mod)
            y = (x - (x * x - N) * inv) % new_mod
            lifted.append(y)
        roots = sorted(set(lifted))
        mod = new_mod
    return roots


def brute_root_count(N: int, m: int) -> int:
    """Number of residues x mod m with x^2 = N (mod m)."""
    return sum(1 for x in range(m) if (x * x - N) % m == 0)


def factorize_small(v: int, primes: List[int]) -> Tuple[Dict[int, int], int]:
    """Trial-divide v by the given primes; return exponents and cofactor."""
    e: Dict[int, int] = {}
    for p in primes:
        while v % p == 0:
            v //= p
            e[p] = e.get(p, 0) + 1
    return e, v


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Hensel lines
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
def section_hensel(N: int) -> None:

    print("1. Sieve lines modulo prime powers p^k  (N = %d)" % N)
    print("=" * 72)
    print(" p  (N|p)   #roots mod p, p^2, p^3   (Hensel)   (brute force)")
    for p in [3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 23]:
        if N % p == 0:
            continue

        brute = [brute_root_count(N, p ** k) for k in (1, 2, 3)]

        assert hens == ([2, 2, 2] if legendre(N, p) == 1 else [0, 0, 0])
    print("Theorem check: exactly 2 lines at every level for residues, 0 for non-residues.\n")


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. The prime 2
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

    print("=" * 72)
    print("2. The 2-adic cap")
    print("=" * 72)
    print("N mod 8 = %d" % (N % 8))
    s = math.isqrt(N) + 1
    max_v2 = 0
    for x in range(s, s + 200000):
        v = x * x - N
        t = 0
        while v % 2 == 0:
            v //= 2
            t += 1
        max_v2 = max(max_v2, t)
    print("max 2-adic valuation of x^2 - N over 200000 consecutive x: %d" % max_v2)
    print("(An odd square is 1 mod 8; N = 3 mod 4 forbids 4 | x^2 - N.)\n")
    assert N % 4 != 3 or max_v2 <= 1


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3 & 4. The toy sieve: exact filter, first-power bug, work count
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
def admissible_factor_base(N: int, B: int) -> List[int]:
    """Primes p <= B that can divide some x^2 - N: p = 2 (N odd) or (N|p) = +1."""
    fb: List[int] = []
    for p in primes_up_to(B):
        if p == 2:
            fb.append(2)
        elif N % p == 0 or legendre(N, p) == 1:
            fb.append(p)
    return fb


def log_sieve(N: int, a: int, M: int, fb: List[int], K: int) -> Tuple[List[float], int]:
    """Log sieve over x in [a, a+M): add log p at every hit of a line mod p^j, j <= K.
    Returns accumulators and the number of log-additions performed."""
    acc = [0.0] * M
    adds = 0
    for p in fb:
        lp = math.log(p)
        for j in range(1, K + 1):
            pj = p ** j
            if pj > (a + M) ** 2:
                break
            if p == 2:
                roots = [x for x in range(pj) if (x * x - N) % pj == 0]
            else:
                roots = hensel_roots(N, p, j)
            if not roots:
                break
            for r in roots:
                start = (r - a) % pj
                for i in range(start, M, pj):
                    acc[i] += lp
                    adds += 1
    return acc, adds


def section_sieve(N: int, B: int, M: int) -> List[Tuple[int, Dict[int, int]]]:
    print("=" * 72)
    print("3/4. Toy sieve over M = %d values above sqrt(N), B = %d" % (M, B))
    print("=" * 72)
    fb = admissible_factor_base(N, B)
    all_primes = primes_up_to(B)
    print("all primes <= B: %d     admissible (QR-restricted) primes: %d" % (len(all_primes), len(fb)))
    print("factor base:", fb)
    a = math.isqrt(N) + 1

    # Ground truth by trial division over ALL primes <= B (the naive method).
    divisions = 0
    truth: List[Tuple[int, Dict[int, int]]] = []
    for i in range(M):
        x = a + i
        v = x * x - N
        e, cof = {}, v
        for p in all_primes:
            divisions += 1
            while cof % p == 0:
                cof //= p
                divisions += 1
                e[p] = e.get(p, 0) + 1
        if cof == 1:
            truth.append((x, e))
    print("trial division: %d divisions (%.1f per value); smooth values: %d"
          % (divisions, divisions / M, len(truth)))
    # Every prime that ever appears is admissible: p | x^2 - N forces (N|p)=+1.
    used = {p for _, e in truth for p in e}
    assert used <= set(fb)
    print("primes actually used by relations are all admissible:", sorted(used))

    def run(K: int) -> Tuple[List[int], int]:
        acc, adds = log_sieve(N, a, M, fb, K)
        surv = [a + i for i in range(M)
                if abs(acc[i] - math.log((a + i) ** 2 - N)) < 1e-6]
        return surv, adds

    Kfull = int(math.log2((a + M) ** 2 - N)) + 1
    surv_full, adds_full = run(Kfull)
    surv_one, adds_one = run(1)
    truth_x = [x for x, _ in truth]
    sqf = [x for x, e in truth if all(c == 1 for c in e.values())]
    print("full sieve (K = %d): %d survivors, %d log-adds (%.2f per value)"
          % (Kfull, len(surv_full), adds_full, adds_full / M))
    print("  survivors == trial-division smooth set?", surv_full == truth_x)
    print("first-power sieve (K = 1): %d survivors" % len(surv_one))
    print("  survivors == squarefree smooth set?    ", surv_one == sqf)
    lost = 1 - len(surv_one) / max(1, len(truth_x))
    print("  fraction of relations lost by the first-power bug: %.1f%%" % (100 * lost))
    assert surv_full == truth_x and surv_one == sqf

    # Survivor-filter cost: additions + trial division of survivors only.
    surv_div = 0
    for x in surv_full:
        _, _ = factorize_small(x * x - N, fb)
        surv_div += len(fb)
    cost_sieve = adds_full + surv_div
    print("sieve cost = %d adds + %d survivor divisions = %d"
          % (adds_full, surv_div, cost_sieve))
    print("advantage (naive divisions / sieve operations) = %.2fx\n" % (divisions / cost_sieve))
    return truth


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Effective u
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
def dickman_rho(u: float, h: float = 1e-3) -> float:
    """Dickman rho by Euler integration of u rho'(u) = -rho(u-1)."""
    if u <= 1:
        return 1.0
    n1 = int(round(1 / h))
    vals = [1.0] * (n1 + 1)
    n = int(round(u / h))
    for i in range(n1 + 1, n + 1):
        t = i * h
        vals.append(vals[-1] - h * vals[i - n1 - 1] / t)
    return vals[n]


def section_effective_u() -> None:
    print("=" * 72)
    print("5. Effective u from the quadratic-residue restriction")
    print("=" * 72)
    print("    B       v        u     factor lnB/(lnB-ln2)   u_eff   rho(u_eff)/rho(u)")
    for B, v in [(60, 10 ** 7), (500, 10 ** 8), (2000, 10 ** 10), (10 ** 4, 10 ** 12)]:
        u = math.log(v) / math.log(B)
        f = math.log(B) / (math.log(B) - math.log(2))
        ueff = math.log(v) / math.log(B / 2)
        assert abs(ueff - u * f) < 1e-12 and ueff > u
        print("%6d  %8.0e  %6.3f   %10.4f            %6.3f   %6.3f"
              % (B, v, u, f, ueff, dickman_rho(ueff) / dickman_rho(u)))
    print("Identity ln v / ln(B/2) = u * lnB/(lnB - ln2) holds; the ratio < 1\n"
          "is the predicted yield shrinkage relative to the plain rho(u) model.\n")


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Linear algebra over GF(2) and the congruence of squares
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
def gf2_dependencies(vectors: List[int], n_rows: int) -> List[int]:
    """Gaussian elimination over GF(2).  vectors[i] is a bitmask of exponent
    parities.  Returns dependencies as bitmasks over relation indices."""
    pivots: Dict[int, Tuple[int, int]] = {}
    deps: List[int] = []
    for i, v in enumerate(vectors):
        comb = 1 << i
        for bit in range(n_rows - 1, -1, -1):
            if not (v >> bit) & 1:
                continue
            if bit in pivots:
                pv, pc = pivots[bit]
                v ^= pv
                comb ^= pc
            else:
                pivots[bit] = (v, comb)
                break
        if v == 0:
            deps.append(comb)
    return deps


def section_factor(N: int, relations: List[Tuple[int, Dict[int, int]]]) -> None:
    print("=" * 72)
    print("6. From relations to a factor")
    print("=" * 72)
    # (a) The certificate quoted in the paper.
    cert = [10248, 10342, 10749, 18185]
    vals = [x * x - N for x in cert]
    prod_v = math.prod(vals)
    Y = math.isqrt(prod_v)
    X = math.prod(cert)
    assert Y * Y == prod_v
    print("certificate abscissae:", cert)
    for x, v in zip(cert, vals):
        print("  %5d^2 - N = %9d = %s" % (x, v, factorize_small(v, primes_up_to(60))[0]))
    print("product of values = Y^2 with Y =", Y)
    print("X = prod x_i =", X, ";  N | X^2 - Y^2 ?", (X * X - Y * Y) % N == 0)
    g = math.gcd(X - Y, N)
    print("gcd(X - Y, N) =", g, "  N / g =", N // g)
    assert g == 9127 and N // g == 11369
    tri = [10342, 10749, 18185]
    Xt = math.prod(tri)
    Yt = math.isqrt(math.prod(x * x - N for x in tri))
    print("3-relation dependency: Y =", Yt, " (X - Y) mod N =", (Xt - Yt) % N, "-> trivial")

    # (b) Live: GF(2) elimination on the relations collected in section 3.
    fb = sorted({p for _, e in relations for p in e})
    idx = {p: j for j, p in enumerate(fb)}
    vecs = []
    for _, e in relations:
        m = 0
        for p, c in e.items():
            if c % 2:
                m |= 1 << idx[p]
        vecs.append(m)
    deps = gf2_dependencies(vecs, len(fb))
    print("\nlive run: %d relations over %d primes -> %d dependencies"
          % (len(relations), len(fb), len(deps)))
    useful = 0
    for d in deps:
        xs = [relations[i][0] for i in range(len(relations)) if (d >> i) & 1]
        Xd = math.prod(xs) % N
        Yd = math.isqrt(math.prod(x * x - N for x in xs)) % N
        g = math.gcd(Xd - Yd, N)
        if 1 < g < N:
            useful += 1
    if deps:
        print("dependencies giving a proper factor: %d / %d  (CRT predicts ~1/2)"
              % (useful, len(deps)))

    # (c) The CRT coin flip: four square roots, two useful.
    p, q = 9127, 11369
    y = 123456 % N
    s = (y * y) % N
    roots_p = [y % p, (-y) % p]
    roots_q = [y % q, (-y) % q]
    roots = sorted({(a * q * pow(q, -1, p) + b * p * pow(p, -1, q)) % N
                    for a in roots_p for b in roots_q})
    print("\nsquare roots of y^2 mod N for y = %d:" % y)
    for r in roots:
        tag = "trivial (+-y)" if r in (y, (-y) % N) else "useful: gcd = %d" % math.gcd(r - y, N)
        assert r * r % N == s
        print("  %9d   %s" % (r, tag))
    assert len(roots) == 4


def main() -> None:
    section_hensel(N_TOY)
    section_two_adic(N_TOY)
    rels = section_sieve(N_TOY, B=60, M=60000)
    section_effective_u()
    section_factor(N_TOY, rels)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

        while v % 2 == 0:
            v //= 2
            t += 1
        max_v2 = max(max_v2, t)
    print("max 2-adic valuation of x^2 - N over 200000 consecutive x: %d" % max_v2)
    print("(An odd square is 1 mod 8; N = 3 mod 4 forbids 4 | x^2 - N.)\n")
    assert N % 4 != 3 or max_v2 <= 1


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3 & 4. The toy sieve: exact filter, first-power bug, work count
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
def admissible_factor_base(N: int, B: int) -> List[int]:
    """Primes p <= B that can divide some x^2 - N: p = 2 (N odd) or (N|p) = +1."""
    fb: List[int] = []
    for p in primes_up_to(B):
        if p == 2:
            fb.append(2)
        elif N % p == 0 or legendre(N, p) == 1:
            fb.append(p)
    return fb


def log_sieve(N: int, a: int, M: int, fb: List[int], K: int) -> Tuple[List[float], int]:
    """Log sieve over x in [a, a+M): add log p at every hit of a line mod p^j, j <= K.
    Returns accumulators and the number of log-additions performed."""
    acc = [0.0] * M
    adds = 0
    for p in fb:
        lp = math.log(p)
        for j in range(1, K + 1):
            pj = p ** j
            if pj > (a + M) ** 2:
                break
            if p == 2:
                roots = [x for x in range(pj) if (x * x - N) % pj == 0]
            else:
                roots = hensel_roots(N, p, j)
            if not roots:
                break
            for r in roots:
                start = (r - a) % pj
                for i in range(start, M, pj):
                    acc[i] += lp
                    adds += 1
    return acc, adds


def section_sieve(N: int, B: int, M: int) -> List[Tuple[int, Dict[int, int]]]:
    print("=" * 72)
    print("3/4. Toy sieve over M = %d values above sqrt(N), B = %d" % (M, B))
    print("=" * 72)
    fb = admissible_factor_base(N, B)
    all_primes = primes_up_to(B)
    print("all primes <= B: %d     admissible (QR-restricted) primes: %d" % (len(all_primes), len(fb)))
    print("factor base:", fb)
    a = math.isqrt(N) + 1

    # Ground truth by trial division over ALL primes <= B (the naive method).
    divisions = 0
    truth: List[Tuple[int, Dict[int, int]]] = []
    for i in range(M):
        x = a + i
        v = x * x - N
        e, cof = {}, v
        for p in all_primes:
            divisions += 1
            while cof % p == 0:
                cof //= p
                divisions += 1
                e[p] = e.get(p, 0) + 1
        if cof == 1:
            truth.append((x, e))
    print("trial division: %d divisions (%.1f per value); smooth values: %d"
          % (divisions, divisions / M, len(truth)))
    # Every prime that ever appears is admissible: p | x^2 - N forces (N|p)=+1.
    used = {p for _, e in truth for p in e}
    assert used <= set(fb)
    print("primes actually used by relations are all admissible:", sorted(used))

    def run(K: int) -> Tuple[List[int], int]:
        acc, adds = log_sieve(N, a, M, fb, K)
        surv = [a + i for i in range(M)
                if abs(acc[i] - math.log((a + i) ** 2 - N)) < 1e-6]
        return surv, adds

    Kfull = int(math.log2((a + M) ** 2 - N)) + 1
    surv_full, adds_full = run(Kfull)
    surv_one, adds_one = run(1)
    truth_x = [x for x, _ in truth]
    sqf = [x for x, e in truth if all(c == 1 for c in e.values())]
    print("full sieve (K = %d): %d survivors, %d log-adds (%.2f per value)"
          % (Kfull, len(surv_full), adds_full, adds_full / M))
    print("  survivors == trial-division smooth set?", surv_full == truth_x)
    print("first-power sieve (K = 1): %d survivors" % len(surv_one))
    print("  survivors == squarefree smooth set?    ", surv_one == sqf)
    lost = 1 - len(surv_one) / max(1, len(truth_x))
    print("  fraction of relations lost by the first-power bug: %.1f%%" % (100 * lost))
    assert surv_full == truth_x and surv_one == sqf

    # Survivor-filter cost: additions + trial division of survivors only.
    surv_div = 0
    for x in surv_full:
        _, _ = factorize_small(x * x - N, fb)
        surv_div += len(fb)
    cost_sieve = adds_full + surv_div
    print("sieve cost = %d adds + %d survivor divisions = %d"
          % (adds_full, surv_div, cost_sieve))
    print("advantage (naive divisions / sieve operations) = %.2fx\n" % (divisions / cost_sieve))
    return truth

# 5. Effective u
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
def dickman_rho(u: float, h: float = 1e-3) -> float:
    """Dickman rho by Euler integration of u rho'(u) = -rho(u-1)."""
    if u <= 1:
        return 1.0
    n1 = int(round(1 / h))
    vals = [1.0] * (n1 + 1)
    n = int(round(u / h))
    for i in range(n1 + 1, n + 1):
        t = i * h
        vals.append(vals[-1] - h * vals[i - n1 - 1] / t)
    return vals[n]


def section_effective_u() -> None:
    print("=" * 72)
    print("5. Effective u from the quadratic-residue restriction")
    print("=" * 72)
    print("    B       v        u     factor lnB/(lnB-ln2)   u_eff   rho(u_eff)/rho(u)")
    for B, v in [(60, 10 ** 7), (500, 10 ** 8), (2000, 10 ** 10), (10 ** 4, 10 ** 12)]:
        u = math.log(v) / math.log(B)
        f = math.log(B) / (math.log(B) - math.log(2))
        ueff = math.log(v) / math.log(B / 2)
        assert abs(ueff - u * f) < 1e-12 and ueff > u
        print("%6d  %8.0e  %6.3f   %10.4f            %6.3f   %6.3f"
              % (B, v, u, f, ueff, dickman_rho(ueff) / dickman_rho(u)))
    print("Identity ln v / ln(B/2) = u * lnB/(lnB - ln2) holds; the ratio < 1\n"
          "is the predicted yield shrinkage relative to the plain rho(u) model.\n")

# 6. Linear algebra over GF(2) and the congruence of squares
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
def gf2_dependencies(vectors: List[int], n_rows: int) -> List[int]:
    """Gaussian elimination over GF(2).  vectors[i] is a bitmask of exponent
    parities.  Returns dependencies as bitmasks over relation indices."""
    pivots: Dict[int, Tuple[int, int]] = {}
    deps: List[int] = []
    for i, v in enumerate(vectors):
        comb = 1 << i
        for bit in range(n_rows - 1, -1, -1):
            if not (v >> bit) & 1:
                continue
            if bit in pivots:
                pv, pc = pivots[bit]
                v ^= pv
                comb ^= pc
            else:
                pivots[bit] = (v, comb)
                break
        if v == 0:
            deps.append(comb)
    return deps


def section_factor(N: int, relations: List[Tuple[int, Dict[int, int]]]) -> None:
    print("=" * 72)
    print("6. From relations to a factor")
    print("=" * 72)
    # (a) The certificate quoted in the paper.
    cert = [10248, 10342, 10749, 18185]
    vals = [x * x - N for x in cert]
    prod_v = math.prod(vals)
    Y = math.isqrt(prod_v)
    X = math.prod(cert)
    assert Y * Y == prod_v
    print("certificate abscissae:", cert)
    for x, v in zip(cert, vals):
        print("  %5d^2 - N = %9d = %s" % (x, v, factorize_small(v, primes_up_to(60))[0]))
    print("product of values = Y^2 with Y =", Y)
    print("X = prod x_i =", X, ";  N | X^2 - Y^2 ?", (X * X - Y * Y) % N == 0)
    g = math.gcd(X - Y, N)
    print("gcd(X - Y, N) =", g, "  N / g =", N // g)
    assert g == 9127 and N // g == 11369
    tri = [10342, 10749, 18185]
    Xt = math.prod(tri)
    Yt = math.isqrt(math.prod(x * x - N for x in tri))
    print("3-relation dependency: Y =", Yt, " (X - Y) mod N =", (Xt - Yt) % N, "-> trivial")

    # (b) Live: GF(2) elimination on the relations collected in section 3.
    fb = sorted({p for _, e in relations for p in e})
    idx = {p: j for j, p in enumerate(fb)}
    vecs = []
    for _, e in relations:
        m = 0
        for p, c in e.items():
            if c % 2:
                m |= 1 << idx[p]
        vecs.append(m)
    deps = gf2_dependencies(vecs, len(fb))
    print("\nlive run: %d relations over %d primes -> %d dependencies"
          % (len(relations), len(fb), len(deps)))
    useful = 0
    for d in deps:
        xs = [relations[i][0] for i in range(len(relations)) if (d >> i) & 1]
        Xd = math.prod(xs) % N
        Yd = math.isqrt(math.prod(x * x - N for x in xs)) % N
        g = math.gcd(Xd - Yd, N)
        if 1 < g < N:

    if deps:
        print("dependencies giving a proper factor: %d / %d  (CRT predicts ~1/2)"
              % (useful, len(deps)))

    # (c) The CRT coin flip: four square roots, two useful.
    p, q = 9127, 11369
    y = 123456 % N
    s = (y * y) % N
    roots_p = [y % p, (-y) % p]

    for r in roots:

        assert r * r % N == s
        print("  %9d   %s" % (r, tag))
    assert len(roots) == 4

from __future__ import annotations
from typing import List


def legendre(a: int, p: int) -> int:
    """Euler's criterion for an odd prime p."""
    t = pow(a % p, (p - 1) // 2, p)
    return -1 if t == p - 1 else t


def tonelli_shanks(n: int, p: int) -> int:
    """Square root of a quadratic residue n modulo an odd prime p."""
    n %= p
    if n == 0:
        return 0
    q, s = p - 1, 0
    while q % 2 == 0:
        q //= 2
        s += 1
    z = 2
    while legendre(z, p) != -1:
        z += 1
    m, c, t, r = s, pow(z, q, p), pow(n, q, p), pow(n, (q + 1) // 2, p)
    while t != 1:
        i, t2 = 0, t
        while t2 != 1:
            t2 = t2 * t2 % p
            i += 1
        b = pow(c, 1 << (m - i - 1), p)
        m, c, t, r = i, b * b % p, t * b * b % p, r * b % p
    return r


def sieve_lines(N: int, p: int, K: int) -> List[List[int]]:
    """For an odd prime p not dividing N return, for k = 1..K, the residues
    x mod p^k with x^2 = N (mod p^k).  Exactly two per level if (N|p) = +1,
    none if (N|p) = -1."""
    if N % p == 0:
        raise ValueError("p divides N")
    if legendre(N, p) == -1:
        return [[] for _ in range(K)]
    r = tonelli_shanks(N, p)
    roots, mod, out = [r, (-r) % p], p, [sorted({r, (-r) % p})]
    for _ in range(1, K):
        new_mod = mod * p
        # the inverse of 2x is recomputed for EACH root at EACH level
        roots = [(x - (x * x - N) * pow(2 * x, -1, new_mod)) % new_mod for x in roots]
        mod = new_mod
        out.append(sorted(set(roots)))
    return out

from __future__ import annotations
import math
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple


def admissible_primes(N: int, B: int) -> List[int]:
    ps = [p for p in range(2, B + 1) if all(p % d for d in range(2, math.isqrt(p) + 1))]
    return [p for p in ps if p == 2 or N % p == 0 or pow(N % p, (p - 1) // 2, p) == 1]


def lines(N: int, p: int, k: int) -> List[int]:
    """Residues x mod p^k with p^k | x^2 - N.  Odd p: a root mod p (brute force)
    lifted by Hensel's step, separately for each root.  p = 2: brute force."""
    if p == 2:
        return [x for x in range(2 ** k) if (x * x - N) % 2 ** k == 0]
    roots = [x for x in range(p) if (x * x - N) % p == 0]
    mod = p
    for _ in range(1, k):
        mod *= p
        roots = [(x - (x * x - N) * pow(2 * x, -1, mod)) % mod for x in roots]
    return sorted(set(roots))


def log_sieve(N: int, B: int, M: int) -> Tuple[List[Tuple[int, Dict[int, int]]], int]:
    """Return the B-smooth relations x^2 - N for x in [ceil sqrt N, +M) and the
    number of log additions.  Height K >= log2(max value) makes the filter exact."""
    a = math.isqrt(N) + 1
    vmax = (a + M) ** 2 - N
    fb = admissible_primes(N, B)
    acc = [0.0] * M
    adds = 0
    for p in fb:
        pk, k = p, 1
        while pk <= vmax:
            rs = lines(N, p, k)
            if not rs:
                break
            for r in rs:
                for i in range((r - a) % pk, M, pk):
                    acc[i] += math.log(p)
                    adds += 1
            pk *= p
            k += 1
    rels: List[Tuple[int, Dict[int, int]]] = []
    for i in range(M):
        x = a + i
        v = x * x - N
        if acc[i] >= math.log(v) - 1e-6:          # survivor
            e: Dict[int, int] = {}
            for p in fb:                          # trial-divide survivors only
                while v % p == 0:
                    v //= p
                    e[p] = e.get(p, 0) + 1
            assert v == 1                         # exact filter: no false positives
            rels.append((x, e))
    return rels, adds

from __future__ import annotations
import math
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple

Relation = Tuple[int, Dict[int, int]]


def dependencies(rels: List[Relation]) -> List[List[int]]:
    """Gaussian elimination over GF(2) on exponent-parity vectors (as int bitmasks)."""
    primes = sorted({p for _, e in rels for p in e})
    col = {p: j for j, p in enumerate(primes)}
    pivots: Dict[int, Tuple[int, int]] = {}
    deps: List[List[int]] = []
    for i, (_, e) in enumerate(rels):
        v = sum(1 << col[p] for p, c in e.items() if c % 2)
        comb = 1 << i
        while v:
            b = v.bit_length() - 1
            if b not in pivots:
                pivots[b] = (v, comb)
                break
            pv, pc = pivots[b]
            v ^= pv
            comb ^= pc
        if v == 0:
            deps.append([j for j in range(len(rels)) if comb >> j & 1])
    return deps


def extract_factor(N: int, rels: List[Relation], dep: List[int]) -> Optional[int]:
    """X = prod x_i, Y = sqrt(prod (x_i^2 - N)) by exponent halving; return a
    proper factor gcd(X - Y, N) or None if X = +-Y (mod N)."""
    X, ex = 1, {}
    for j in dep:
        x, e = rels[j]
        X = X * x % N
        for p, c in e.items():
            ex[p] = ex.get(p, 0) + c
    Y = 1
    for p, c in ex.items():
        assert c % 2 == 0
        Y = Y * pow(p, c // 2, N) % N
    assert (X * X - Y * Y) % N == 0               # congruence of squares
    g = math.gcd(X - Y, N)
    return g if 1 < g < N else None

<script>
const $ = id => document.getElementById(id);
document.querySelectorAll('.tab').forEach(t => t.onclick = () => {
  document.querySelectorAll('.tab').forEach(x => x.classList.remove('on'));
  document.querySelectorAll('section').forEach(x => x.classList.remove('on'));
  t.classList.add('on'); $(t.dataset.t).classList.add('on');
});
let mode = 'full';
document.querySelectorAll('#kseg div').forEach(d => d.onclick = () => {
  document.querySelectorAll('#kseg div').forEach(x => x.classList.remove('on'));
  d.classList.add('on'); mode = d.dataset.k; run();

const big = BigInt;
function mod(a, m) { a %= m; return a < 0n ? a + m : a; }
function powmod(b, e, m) { b = mod(b, m); let r = 1n; while (e > 0n) { if (e & 1n) r = r * b % m; b = b * b % m; e >>= 1n; } return r; }
function egcd(a, b) { let [x0, x1, y0, y1] = [1n, 0n, 0n, 1n]; while (b) { const q = a / b; [a, b] = [b, a % b]; [x0, x1] = [x1, x0 - q * x1]; [y0, y1] = [y1, y0 - q * y1]; } return [a, x0, y0]; }
function inv(a, m) { const [g, x] = egcd(mod(a, m), m); return g === 1n ? mod(x, m) : null; }
function gcd(a, b) { a = a < 0n ? -a : a; b = b < 0n ? -b : b; while (b) [a, b] = [b, a % b]; return a; }
function isqrt(n) { if (n < 2n) return n; let x = big(Math.floor(Math.sqrt(Number(n)))); while (x * x > n) x--; while ((x + 1n) * (x + 1n) <= n) x++; return x; }
function primes(n) { const s = new Uint8Array(n + 1), out = []; for (let i = 2; i <= n; i++) { if (!s[i]) { out.push(i); for (let j = i * i; j <= n; j += i) s[j] = 1; } } return out; }
function legendre(N, p) { const t = powmod(N, big((p - 1) / 2), big(p)); return t === 0n ? 0 : (t === 1n ? 1 : -1); }

function henselRoots(N, p, k) {
  const P = big(p); let r = null;
  for (let x = 0n; x < P; x++) if (mod(x * x - N, P) === 0n) { r = x; break; }
  if (r === null) return [];
  let roots = [...new Set([r, mod(-r, P)].map(String))].map(big), m = P;
  for (let j = 1; j < k; j++) {
    const m2 = m * P;
    roots = [...new Set(roots.map(x => String(mod(x - (x * x - N) * inv(2n * x, m2), m2))))].map(big);
    m = m2;
  }
  return roots;
}

let STATE = null;
function run() {
  const N = big($('N').value), B = Math.max(3, +$('B').value), M = Math.min(400000, Math.max(100, +$('M').value));
  const allP = primes(B);
  const fb = allP.filter(p => p === 2 || legendre(N, p) !== -1);
  $('chips').innerHTML = allP.map(p => `<span class="${fb.includes(p) ? 'qr' : 'nqr'}">${p}</span>`).join('');
  const a = isqrt(N) + 1n, aN = Number(a), Nn = Number(N);
  const vmax = Number((a + big(M)) ** 2n - N);
  const Kfull = Math.ceil(Math.log2(vmax)) + 1;
  const acc = new Float64Array(M); let adds = 0;
  for (const p of fb) {
    const lp = Math.log(p);
    const Kp = mode === '1' ? 1 : Kfull;
    for (let k = 1; k <= Kp; k++) {
      const pk = p ** k; if (pk > vmax) break;
      let roots;
      if (p === 2) { roots = []; for (let x = 0; x < pk && pk <= 1 << 20; x++) if (mod(big(x) * big(x) - N, big(pk)) === 0n) roots.push(big(x)); }
      else roots = henselRoots(N, p, k);
      if (!roots.length) break;
      for (const r of roots) { let s = Number(mod(r - a, big(pk))); for (let i = s; i < M; i += pk) { acc[i] += lp; adds++; } }
    }
  }
  const val = i => Number((a + big(i)) ** 2n - N);
  const surv = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < M; i++) if (acc[i] >= Math.log(val(i)) - 1e-7) surv.push(i);
  // trial division ground truth
  const rels = []; let divs = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < M; i++) {
    let v = val(i); const e = {};
    for (const p of allP) { divs++; while (v % p === 0) { v /= p; e[p] = (e[p] || 0) + 1; divs++; } }
    if (v === 1) rels.push({ i, x: a + big(i), v: val(i), e, sqf: Object.values(e).every(c => c === 1) });
  }
  const sqf = rels.filter(r => r.sqf).length;
  const survCost = adds + surv.length * fb.length;
  $('stats').innerHTML =
    `<span class="stat">relations (trial division)<br><b>${rels.length}</b></span>` +
    `<span class="stat">survivors of this sieve<br><b>${surv.length}</b></span>` +
    `<span class="stat">squarefree among relations<br><b>${sqf}</b></span>` +
    `<span class="stat">divisions / value (naive)<br><b>${(divs / M).toFixed(1)}</b></span>` +
    `<span class="stat">log-adds / value (sieve)<br><b>${(adds / M).toFixed(2)}</b></span>` +
    `<span class="stat">advantage<br><b>${(divs / survCost).toFixed(1)}×</b></span>` +
    `<div class="note" style="margin-top:8px">${mode === '1'
      ? `First powers only: survivors = squarefree smooth values exactly. Lost: <b style="color:var(--bad)">${rels.length - surv.length}</b> of ${rels.length} relations (${rels.length ? (100 * (rels.length - surv.length) / rels.length).toFixed(0) : 0}%).`
      : `Exact sieve (height ${Kfull} ≥ log₂ v): survivors coincide with the trial-division smooth set: <b style="color:var(--good)">${surv.length === rels.length && surv.every((s, j) => s === rels[j].i)}</b>.`}</div>`;
  $('rel').innerHTML = '<tr><th>x</th><th>x² − N</th><th>factorization</th><th>survives?</th></tr>' + rels.map(r =>
    `<tr><td>${r.x}</td><td>${r.v}</td><td class="${r.sqf ? 'sq' : 'nsq'}">${Object.entries(r.e).map(([p, c]) => c > 1 ? `${p}<sup>${c}</sup>` : p).join(' · ')}</td><td>${surv.includes(r.i) ? '✓' : '<span style="color:var(--bad)">lost</span>'}</td></tr>`).join('');
  draw(acc, val, Math.min(600, M), new Set(rels.map(r => r.i)));
  STATE = { N, rels: rels.map(r => ({ x: r.x, e: r.e })) };
}

function draw(acc, val, L, relSet) {
  const cv = $('cv'), g = cv.getContext('2d'), W = cv.width, H = cv.height;
  g.clearRect(0, 0, W, H);
  const bw = W / L, base = H - 14, sc = (H - 34);
  g.strokeStyle = '#ff6b8a'; g.setLineDash([5, 4]); g.beginPath(); g.moveTo(0, base - sc); g.lineTo(W, base - sc); g.stroke(); g.setLineDash([]);
  g.fillStyle = '#9aa3c7'; g.font = '11px sans-serif'; g.fillText('threshold = log v', 6, base - sc - 4);
  for (let i = 0; i < L; i++) {
    const r = acc[i] / Math.log(val(i));
    g.fillStyle = r >= 1 - 1e-9 ? '#5be3a1' : (relSet.has(i) ? '#ffb86b' : '#3b4a86');
    g.fillRect(i * bw, base - Math.min(1.05, r) * sc, Math.max(1, bw - .3), Math.min(1.05, r) * sc);
  }
  cv.onmousemove = ev => {
    const rect = cv.getBoundingClientRect(); const i = Math.floor((ev.clientX - rect.left) / rect.width * L);
    if (i >= 0 && i < L) $('hover').innerHTML = `offset ${i}: v = ${val(i)}, accumulated ${acc[i].toFixed(3)} of log v = ${Math.log(val(i)).toFixed(3)} (${(100 * acc[i] / Math.log(val(i))).toFixed(1)}%)${relSet.has(i) ? ' — <b>smooth</b>' : ''}`;
  };
}

function factor() {
  if (!STATE) run();
  const { N, rels } = STATE;
  if (rels.length < 2) { $('facout').innerHTML = 'Not enough relations. Enlarge M or B.'; return; }
  const ps = [...new Set(rels.flatMap(r => Object.keys(r.e).map(Number)))].sort((x, y) => x - y);
  const idx = Object.fromEntries(ps.map((p, j) => [p, j]));
  const piv = new Map(), deps = [];
  rels.forEach((r, i) => {
    let v = 0n, c = 1n << big(i);
    for (const [p, e] of Object.entries(r.e)) if (e % 2) v |= 1n << big(idx[p]);
    for (let b = ps.length - 1; b >= 0; b--) {
      if (!((v >> big(b)) & 1n)) continue;
      if (piv.has(b)) { const [pv, pc] = piv.get(b); v ^= pv; c ^= pc; } else { piv.set(b, [v, c]); break; }
    }
    if (v === 0n) deps.push(c);
  });
  let html = `<div class="note">${rels.length} relations over ${ps.length} primes ⇒ at least ${Math.max(0, rels.length - ps.length)} dependencies guaranteed; found ${deps.length}.</div><table><tr><th>#</th><th>relations used</th><th>X − Y mod N</th><th>gcd(X − Y, N)</th><th>verdict</th></tr>`;
  let useful = 0;
  deps.slice(0, 30).forEach((d, k) => {
    const used = rels.filter((_, i) => (d >> big(i)) & 1n);
    const ex = {}; used.forEach(r => { for (const [p, e] of Object.entries(r.e)) ex[p] = (ex[p] || 0) + e; });
    let X = 1n, Y = 1n;
    used.forEach(r => X = X * r.x % N);
    for (const [p, e] of Object.entries(ex)) Y = Y * powmod(big(p), big(e / 2), N) % N;
    const g = gcd(mod(X - Y, N), N);
    const ok = g > 1n && g < N; if (ok) useful++;

  "interactive_layout": "# Inside the Quadratic Sieve: where the speed comes from, and why the harvest is thinner than expected

The quadratic sieve factors a number $N$ by collecting **relations**: integers $x$ just above $\sqrt N$ for which $x^2 - N$ breaks completely into small primes. This page takes a toy version apart. Our running example is

$$N = 103\,764\,863 = 9127 \times 11369.$$

We'll answer two questions on the way:

1. **Why is sieving faster than trial division?** Is it a fixed factor, or does the advantage grow with scale?
2. **How many relations should we expect?** Does the classical Dickman estimate $\rho(u)$ apply to $x^2 - N$?

<details><summary>Background: smooth numbers and Dickman's function</summary>

A positive integer is **$B$-smooth** if all its prime factors are at most $B$. For a random integer of size $v$, the probability of being $B$-smooth is roughly $\rho(u)$ with $u = \ln v / \ln B$. Here $\rho$ is [Dickman's function](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dickman_function): $\rho(u) = 1$ for $u \le 1$ and $u\rho'(u) = -\rho(u-1)$ after that. It drops quickly, with $\rho(2) \approx 0.31$, $\rho(3) \approx 0.049$ and $\rho(4) \approx 0.0049$. See also [smooth numbers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smooth_number) and the [quadratic sieve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quadratic_sieve).
</details>

## 1. Primes walk in straight lines

If $p \mid x^2 - N$, then $p \mid (x+p)^2 - N$ as well. So each prime hits the values $x^2 - N$ along arithmetic progressions, the **sieve lines**. How many lines are there modulo $p^k$?

> **Theorem (exactly two lines, or none).** Let $p$ be an odd prime with $p \nmid N$. If $N$ is a quadratic residue mod $p$, i.e. $(N\mid p) = +1$, then $x^2 \equiv N \pmod{p^k}$ has *exactly two* solutions for every $k \ge 1$. If $(N \mid p) = -1$, it has *none* at any level.

<details><summary>Proof sketch (Hensel lifting)</summary>

*Existence.* Given a root $x$ modulo $p^k$ with $x^2 - N = p^k c$, try $y = x + tp^k$. Then $y^2 - N = p^k(c + 2xt) + t^2 p^{2k}$, and we need $c + 2xt \equiv 0 \pmod p$. That is solvable because $2x$ is a unit ($p$ is odd and $p \nmid x$, since $p \nmid N$).

*At most two.* If $x$ and $y$ are both roots, then $p^k \mid (x-y)(x+y)$. The prime $p$ can't divide both factors (it would then divide $2x$, hence $N$), so $p^k$ divides one of them: $y \equiv \pm x$.

*Non-residues.* A root mod $p^k$ reduces to a root mod $p$, and there is none.
</details>

So about **half of all primes can never appear** in any relation. For our $N$, only 10 of the 17 primes up to 60 are admissible: $\{2, 11, 17, 19, 23, 31, 37, 43, 47, 59\}$. The prime $2$ is special. Odd squares are $1 \bmod 8$, and since $N \equiv 7 \pmod 8$, no value $x^2 - N$ is ever divisible by $4$.

{{algorithm:0}}

## 2. The sieve is a filter, and it is exact

Instead of trial-dividing each value, the sieve walks every line and adds $\log p$ at each hit. A value whose total reaches $\log v$ **survives**, and only survivors are trial-divided. Try it below. The green chips are admissible primes and the red ones never occur. Flip between the *exact* sieve and the *first powers only* sieve and watch relations disappear.

{{interactive_demo:0}}

What does the threshold accept? There is a clean answer.

> **Theorem (exact acceptance).** With prime-power lines up to height $K$, the accumulator at $v$ equals $\sum_{p \in S} \min(v_p(v), K)\log p$. It reaches $\log v$ **iff** $v$ is $S$-smooth with every exponent $\le K$.
>
> * With $K = 1$, the survivors are **exactly the squarefree smooth values**. Every relation with a repeated prime factor is lost, with a strict log deficit.
> * With $K \ge \log_2 v$, the survivors are **exactly** the smooth values that trial division finds: no losses, no false positives.

<details><summary>Proof sketch</summary>

The number of $k \le K$ with $p^k \mid v$ is $\min(v_p(v),K)$. So the accumulator is the log of $P = \prod_{p\in S} p^{\min(v_p(v),K)}$, a divisor of $v$. Then $\log P = \log v$ iff $P = v$ iff every valuation is matched. With $K \ge \log_2 v \ge v_p(v)$ the cap never binds.
</details>

{{visualization:0}}

{{algorithm:1}}

### How big is the advantage?

Count the operations. Trial division costs about $\pi(B)$ divisions per value. The sieve's work is bounded by a theorem:

> **Theorem (sieve work).** Over a window of $M$ consecutive $x$, a height-$K$ sieve performs at most $\displaystyle\sum_{p \in S}\sum_{k=1}^{K} 2\left(\frac{M}{p^k} + 1\right)$ log additions.

<details><summary>Why</summary>

A window of $M$ integers contains at most $M/m + 1$ members of a residue class mod $m$, and each $p^k$ has at most two classes.
</details>

Per value that is about $2\sum 1/(p-1)$, which is just a few additions. In six experimental settings ($N$ up to $2^{32}$) the measured advantage was **$13.7\times$ to $20.5\times$**, flat relative to the factor-base size ($0.12$ to $0.22$), with no growth with scale. Roughly *a hundred divisions per value became about two additions per value*. The advantage is the survivor filter and nothing more.

<details><summary>Lab note: the bug only brute force could catch</summary>

An early sieve marked lines modulo $p$ only. Its built-in self-check predicted yield using the *same* omission, so it agreed with the buggy code. Only an independent brute-force recount exposed the missing relations (under an exact threshold, 54–91% of all relations, as the theorem predicts). A second bug, a modular inverse computed once instead of once per root, was caught the same way. After the fixes, a brute-force subrange matched 338 of 338 relations. **A check that shares the code's assumptions cannot falsify them.**
</details>

## 3. The harvest is thinner than random

The textbook model treats $x^2 - N$ as a random integer and predicts a yield of about $0.90\,\rho(u)$. At $u \approx 3$ that model **overpredicted by about $1.55\times$**, and all six settings fell outside the band.

The reason is Section 1. Smoothness of $x^2 - N$ is decided over the **quadratic-residue-restricted** pool of primes. A rough correction treats the bound as $B/2$:

$$u_{\mathrm{eff}} = \frac{\ln v}{\ln(B/2)} = u\cdot\frac{\ln B}{\ln B - \ln 2} > u.$$

This predicted yield ratios of $0.44$ to $0.52$. The observed ratios were $0.54$ to $0.76$, with correlation $0.72$ across settings. The direction is right and the size is overcorrected, because each admissible prime hits along *two* lines, which partly compensates.

{{visualization:1}}

## 4. From relations to a factor

> **Facts.** (i) $\left(\prod x_i\right)^2 \equiv \prod (x_i^2 - N) \pmod N$. (ii) More relations than admissible primes force a subset with square product $Y^2$ (linear algebra over $\mathbb F_2$). (iii) If $X^2 \equiv Y^2$ but $X \not\equiv \pm Y$, then $\gcd(X - Y, N)$ is a proper factor.

> **Theorem (CRT coin flip).** For $N = pq$ with $p \ne q$ odd primes and $y$ a unit, $x^2 \equiv y^2 \pmod N$ has exactly **4** roots, and exactly **2** of them are not $\pm y$.

<details><summary>Proof sketch</summary>

$\mathbb Z/pq \cong \mathbb Z/p \times \mathbb Z/q$. In each field $a^2 = b^2 \iff a = \pm b$, and $b \ne -b$ in odd characteristic. So the roots are $\{\pm y_p\} \times \{\pm y_q\}$. The two same-sign choices are $\pm y$, and the two mixed-sign choices are the useful ones.
</details>

Use tabs 2 and 3 of the widget above to watch this happen. For our $N$, the dependency $\{10342, 10749, 18185\}$ is **trivial** ($X \equiv Y$), while

| $x$ | $x^2 - N$ |
|---|---|
| 10248 | $19^2\cdot 59^2$ |
| 10342 | $11^2\cdot 23\cdot 31\cdot 37$ |
| 10749 | $2\cdot 11\cdot 17\cdot 23\cdot 37^2$ |
| 18185 | $2\cdot 11\cdot 17\cdot 23^2\cdot 31\cdot 37$ |

multiplies to $Y^2$ with $Y = 103\,535\,840\,624\,414$ and gives $\gcd(X - Y, N) = 9127$. **Every one of these four relations has a repeated prime factor**, so the first-power sieve would have missed all of them. (The first row is also a perfect square by itself, $1121^2$, which is Fermat's method appearing inside the sieve.)

{{algorithm:2}}

/-!
# From relations to a factor: congruence of squares, the CRT coin flip, and `N = 103764863`

Context (experiment 470, stretch goal).  The toy sieve's relations were pushed
through `𝔽₂` elimination and actually factored `N = 103764863 = 9127 × 11369`.
The dependency search itself is `QSDimension.qs_congruence_of_squares`.  This file
supplies the remaining links of the chain, and the CRT fact governing how often a
dependency is useful.

* `prod_relations_congr` — the product of the relation values `xᵢ² - N` over any
  subset is congruent to `(∏ xᵢ)²` modulo `N`;
* `gcd_nontrivial_of_sq_congr` — a congruence of squares `X² ≡ Y²` with
  `X ≢ ±Y (mod N)` yields a proper divisor `gcd(X - Y, N)`;
* `qs_factor_of_dependency` — end-to-end: a square dependency among relations
  that is not of the trivial form `X ≡ ±Y` factors `N`;
* `card_sqrt_sq_semiprime` / `card_nontrivial_sqrt_semiprime` — **the CRT coin
  flip**: for `N = p q` (distinct odd primes) a unit square has exactly `4` square
  roots modulo `N`, exactly `2` of which are non-trivial.  This explains the toy
  run's observation that the 3-relation dependencies were trivial while the
  4-relation ones factored `N`;
* Lab notes: the actual certificate for `N = 103764863` from the toy run, checked
  through the theorems above.

namespace ToyQSFactor

open Finset

/-- **Relations multiply to a congruence of squares.**  For any finite family of
sieve abscissae `xᵢ`, `N ∣ (∏ xᵢ)² - ∏ (xᵢ² - N)`. -/
theorem prod_relations_congr {ι : Type*} (T : Finset ι) (X : ι → ℤ) (N : ℤ) :
    N ∣ (∏ i ∈ T, X i) ^ 2 - ∏ i ∈ T, (X i ^ 2 - N) := by
  classical
  induction T using Finset.induction_on with
  | empty => simp
  | insert j T hj ih =>
    rw [Finset.prod_insert hj, Finset.prod_insert hj]
    obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := ih
    refine ⟨X j ^ 2 * c + ∏ i ∈ T, (X i ^ 2 - N), ?_⟩
    have e : (X j * ∏ i ∈ T, X i) ^ 2 - (X j ^ 2 - N) * ∏ i ∈ T, (X i ^ 2 - N)
        = X j ^ 2 * ((∏ i ∈ T, X i) ^ 2 - ∏ i ∈ T, (X i ^ 2 - N))
          + N * ∏ i ∈ T, (X i ^ 2 - N) := by ring
    rw [e, hc]; ring

/-- **Factor extraction.**  If `N ∣ X² - Y²` but `N ∤ X - Y` and `N ∤ X + Y`, then
`gcd(X - Y, N)` is a proper divisor of `N`. -/
theorem gcd_nontrivial_of_sq_congr {N X Y : ℤ} (h : N ∣ X ^ 2 - Y ^ 2)
    (h1 : ¬ N ∣ X - Y) (h2 : ¬ N ∣ X + Y) :
    1 < Int.gcd (X - Y) N ∧ Int.gcd (X - Y) N < N.natAbs := by
  have hprod : N ∣ (X - Y) * (X + Y) := by
    have e : X ^ 2 - Y ^ 2 = (X - Y) * (X + Y) := by ring
    rwa [← e]
  have hN : N ≠ 0 := by
    rintro rfl
    rw [zero_dvd_iff, mul_eq_zero] at hprod
    rcases hprod with h' | h' <;> simp_all
  set g := Int.gcd (X - Y) N with hg
  have hgdvd : (g : ℤ) ∣ N := Int.gcd_dvd_right _ _
  have hgle : g ≤ N.natAbs := Nat.le_of_dvd (Int.natAbs_pos.2 hN) (by
    have := Int.natAbs_dvd_natAbs.2 hgdvd; simpa using this)
  refine ⟨?_, lt_of_le_of_ne hgle ?_⟩
  · by_contra hlt
    push_neg at hlt
    have hg0 : g ≠ 0 := by
      intro h0
      exact hN (Int.gcd_eq_zero_iff.1 h0).2
    have hg1 : g = 1 := by omega
    have hcop : IsCoprime N (X - Y) := by
      rw [Int.isCoprime_iff_gcd_eq_one, Int.gcd_comm]; exact hg1
    exact h2 (hcop.dvd_of_dvd_mul_left hprod)
  · intro heq
    apply h1
    have : (N.natAbs : ℤ) ∣ X - Y := by
      rw [← heq]; exact Int.gcd_dvd_left _ _
    exact (Int.natAbs_dvd.1 this)

/-- **End-to-end factoring from a square dependency.**  Let `xᵢ` (`i ∈ T`) be sieve
abscissae whose relation values multiply to a square `Y²`.  If the dependency is
not trivial (`∏ xᵢ ≢ ±Y mod N`), then `gcd(∏ xᵢ - Y, N)` is a proper factor. -/
theorem qs_factor_of_dependency {ι : Type*} (T : Finset ι) (X : ι → ℤ) {N Y : ℤ}
    (hsq : ∏ i ∈ T, (X i ^ 2 - N) = Y ^ 2)
    (h1 : ¬ N ∣ (∏ i ∈ T, X i) - Y) (h2 : ¬ N ∣ (∏ i ∈ T, X i) + Y) :
    1 < Int.gcd ((∏ i ∈ T, X i) - Y) N ∧ Int.gcd ((∏ i ∈ T, X i) - Y) N < N.natAbs := by
  have := prod_relations_congr T X N
  rw [hsq] at this
  exact gcd_nontrivial_of_sq_congr this h1 h2

/-- **Existence of a dependency from enough relations** (re-export of the catalog
dimension bound in the form used here): more `B`-smooth relations than admissible
primes always contain a nonempty sub-family with square product. -/
theorem exists_square_dependency {B : ℕ} {N : ℤ} {n : ℕ} (X : Fin n → ℤ) (V : Fin n → ℕ)
    (hV0 : ∀ i, V i ≠ 0) (hval : ∀ i, (V i : ℤ) = (X i) ^ 2 - N)
    (hsm : ∀ i, ∀ p ∈ (V i).primeFactors, p ≤ B)
    (hcard : (QSDimension.admissiblePrimes N B).card < n) :
    ∃ T : Finset (Fin n), T.Nonempty ∧ ∃ Y : ℤ, ∏ i ∈ T, (X i ^ 2 - N) = Y ^ 2 ∧
      N ∣ (∏ i ∈ T, X i) ^ 2 - Y ^ 2 := by
  obtain ⟨T, hT, ⟨m, hm⟩⟩ := QSDimension.qs_congruence_of_squares X V hV0 hval hsm hcard
  have e : ∏ i ∈ T, (X i ^ 2 - N) = (m : ℤ) ^ 2 := by
    rw [← Finset.prod_congr rfl (fun i _ => hval i), ← Nat.cast_prod, hm]
    push_cast; ring
  refine ⟨T, hT, m, e, ?_⟩
  have h := prod_relations_congr T X N
  rwa [e] at h

/-! ## The CRT coin flip for `N = p q` -/

section CRT

variable {p q : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] [Fact q.Prime]

/-- In `ZMod p` (`p` odd prime) a nonzero element differs from its negative. -/
lemma ne_neg_of_ne_zero (hp : p ≠ 2) {a : ZMod p} (ha : a ≠ 0) : a ≠ -a := by
  intro h
  have h2 : (2 : ZMod p) * a = 0 := by linear_combination h
  rcases mul_eq_zero.1 h2 with h2 | h2
  · have : ((2 : ℕ) : ZMod p) = 0 := by exact_mod_cast h2
    rw [ZMod.natCast_eq_zero_iff] at this
    exact hp ((Nat.prime_dvd_prime_iff_eq Fact.out Nat.prime_two).1 this)
  · exact ha h2

/-- Square roots of `w²` in a product of two fields: the four sign patterns. -/
lemma sqrt_set_prod (w : ZMod p × ZMod q) :
    {z : ZMod p × ZMod q | z ^ 2 = w ^ 2} = ({w.1, -w.1} : Set (ZMod p)) ×ˢ {w.2, -w.2} := by
  ext ⟨a, b⟩
  simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_prod, Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff,
    Prod.ext_iff, Prod.pow_fst, Prod.pow_snd, sq_eq_sq_iff_eq_or_eq_neg]

/-- **Four square roots.**  For distinct odd primes `p ≠ q` and a unit `y` modulo
`N = p q`, the congruence `x² ≡ y² (mod N)` has exactly `4` solutions. -/
theorem card_sqrt_sq_semiprime (hp : p ≠ 2) (hq : q ≠ 2) (hpq : p ≠ q)
    {y : ZMod (p * q)} (hy : IsUnit y) :
    {x : ZMod (p * q) | x ^ 2 = y ^ 2}.ncard = 4 := by
  have hcop : Nat.Coprime p q := (Nat.coprime_primes Fact.out Fact.out).2 hpq
  set e := ZMod.chineseRemainder hcop
  have hey : IsUnit (e y) := hy.map e
  have h1 : (e y).1 ≠ 0 := (Prod.isUnit_iff.1 hey).1.ne_zero
  have h2 : (e y).2 ≠ 0 := (Prod.isUnit_iff.1 hey).2.ne_zero
  have himg : e.toEquiv '' {x : ZMod (p * q) | x ^ 2 = y ^ 2}
      = {z : ZMod p × ZMod q | z ^ 2 = (e y) ^ 2} := by
    ext z
    simp only [Set.mem_image, Set.mem_setOf_eq]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩
      change e x ^ 2 = e y ^ 2
      rw [← map_pow, ← map_pow, hx]
    · intro hz
      refine ⟨e.symm z, ?_, by simp⟩
      apply e.injective
      rw [map_pow, map_pow, RingEquiv.apply_symm_apply, hz]
  rw [← Set.ncard_image_of_injective _ e.toEquiv.injective, himg, sqrt_set_prod,
    Set.ncard_prod, Set.ncard_pair (ne_neg_of_ne_zero hp h1),
    Set.ncard_pair (ne_neg_of_ne_zero hq h2)]

/-- **Exactly half the square roots are useful.**  Of the four roots of
`x² ≡ y² (mod p q)`, exactly two are different from `±y`; each of those yields a
proper factor via `gcd_nontrivial_of_sq_congr`.  Heuristically each independent
dependency therefore factors `N` with probability `1/2`. -/
theorem card_nontrivial_sqrt_semiprime (hp : p ≠ 2) (hq : q ≠ 2) (hpq : p ≠ q)
    {y : ZMod (p * q)} (hy : IsUnit y) :
    {x : ZMod (p * q) | x ^ 2 = y ^ 2 ∧ x ≠ y ∧ x ≠ -y}.ncard = 2 := by
  have hcop : Nat.Coprime p q := (Nat.coprime_primes Fact.out Fact.out).2 hpq
  set e := ZMod.chineseRemainder hcop
  have hey : IsUnit (e y) := hy.map e
  have h1 : (e y).1 ≠ 0 := (Prod.isUnit_iff.1 hey).1.ne_zero
  have h2 : (e y).2 ≠ 0 := (Prod.isUnit_iff.1 hey).2.ne_zero
  have hn1 := ne_neg_of_ne_zero hp h1
  have hn2 := ne_neg_of_ne_zero hq h2
  have himg : e.toEquiv '' {x : ZMod (p * q) | x ^ 2 = y ^ 2 ∧ x ≠ y ∧ x ≠ -y}
      = {((e y).1, -(e y).2), (-(e y).1, (e y).2)} := by
    have key : ∀ z : ZMod p × ZMod q,
        (e.symm z ^ 2 = y ^ 2 ∧ e.symm z ≠ y ∧ e.symm z ≠ -y) ↔
          (z ^ 2 = (e y) ^ 2 ∧ z ≠ e y ∧ z ≠ -(e y)) := by
      intro z
      have hs : e.symm z ^ 2 = y ^ 2 ↔ z ^ 2 = (e y) ^ 2 := by
        constructor
        · intro h; rw [← RingEquiv.apply_symm_apply e z, ← map_pow, h, map_pow]
        · intro h; apply e.injective; rw [map_pow, map_pow, RingEquiv.apply_symm_apply, h]
      have hy1 : e.symm z ≠ y ↔ z ≠ e y := by
        constructor
        · intro h h'; apply h; rw [h']; simp
        · intro h h'; apply h; rw [← h']; simp
      have hy2 : e.symm z ≠ -y ↔ z ≠ -(e y) := by
        constructor
        · intro h h'; apply h; rw [h', ← map_neg]; simp
        · intro h h'; apply h; rw [← RingEquiv.apply_symm_apply e z, h', map_neg]
      rw [hs, hy1, hy2]
    ext ⟨a, b⟩
    rw [Equiv.image_eq_preimage_symm]
    simp only [Set.mem_preimage, Set.mem_setOf_eq]
    change (e.symm (a, b) ^ 2 = y ^ 2 ∧ e.symm (a, b) ≠ y ∧ e.symm (a, b) ≠ -y) ↔ _
    rw [key]
    simp only [Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff, Prod.ext_iff, Prod.pow_fst,
      Prod.pow_snd, Prod.fst_neg, Prod.snd_neg, ne_eq, sq_eq_sq_iff_eq_or_eq_neg, not_and]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨⟨ha | ha, hb | hb⟩, hne1, hne2⟩
      · exact absurd hb (hne1 ha)
      · exact Or.inl ⟨ha, hb⟩
      · exact Or.inr ⟨ha, hb⟩
      · exact absurd hb (hne2 ha)
    · rintro (⟨ha, hb⟩ | ⟨ha, hb⟩)
      · refine ⟨⟨Or.inl ha, Or.inr hb⟩, fun _ h => hn2 (h.symm.trans hb), fun h _ => ?_⟩
        exact hn1 (ha.symm.trans h)
      · refine ⟨⟨Or.inr ha, Or.inl hb⟩, fun h _ => hn1 (h.symm.trans ha), fun _ h => ?_⟩
        exact hn2 (hb.symm.trans h)
  rw [← Set.ncard_image_of_injective _ e.toEquiv.injective, himg, Set.ncard_pair]
  intro h

from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple

# Elementary number theory

def primes_up_to(n: int) -> List[int]:
    """Sieve of Eratosthenes."""
    if n < 2:
        return []
    is_p = bytearray([1]) * (n + 1)
    is_p[0] = is_p[1] = 0
    for i in range(2, math.isqrt(n) + 1):
        if is_p[i]:
            is_p[i * i :: i] = bytearray(len(is_p[i * i :: i]))
    return [i for i in range(n + 1) if is_p[i]]


def legendre(a: int, p: int) -> int:
    """Legendre symbol (a | p) for an odd prime p, via Euler's criterion."""
    t = pow(a % p, (p - 1) // 2, p)
    return -1 if t == p - 1 else t


def sqrt_mod_prime(a: int, p: int) -> Optional[int]:
    """A square root of a modulo the odd prime p (brute force; p is small)."""
    a %= p
    for x in range(p):
        if x * x % p == a:
            return x
    return None


def hensel_roots(N: int, p: int, k: int) -> List[int]:
    """All roots of x^2 = N (mod p^k), p odd, p not dividing N.
    Lifts each root mod p step by step: y = x - (x^2 - N) * (2x)^{-1} mod p^{j+1}."""
    r = sqrt_mod_prime(N, p)
    if r is None:
        return []
    roots = sorted({r, (-r) % p})
    mod = p
    for _ in range(1, k):
        new_mod = mod * p
        lifted = []
        for x in roots:
            inv = pow(2 * x, -1, new_mod)
            y = (x - (x * x - N) * inv) % new_mod
            lifted.append(y)
        roots = sorted(set(lifted))
        mod = new_mod
    return roots


def brute_root_count(N: int, m: int) -> int:
    """Number of residues x mod m with x^2 = N (mod m)."""
    return sum(1 for x in range(m) if (x * x - N) % m == 0)


def factorize_small(v: int, primes: List[int]) -> Tuple[Dict[int, int], int]:
    """Trial-divide v by the given primes; return exponents and cofactor."""
    e: Dict[int, int] = {}
    for p in primes:
        while v % p == 0:
            v //= p
            e[p] = e.get(p, 0) + 1
    return e, v

def section_hensel(N: int) -> None:
    print("=" * 72)
    print("1. Sieve lines modulo prime powers p^k  (N = %d)" % N)
    print("=" * 72)
    print(" p  (N|p)   #roots mod p, p^2, p^3   (Hensel)   (brute force)")

# 3 & 4. The toy sieve: exact filter, first-power bug, work count
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
def admissible_factor_base(N: int, B: int) -> List[int]:
    """Primes p <= B that can divide some x^2 - N: p = 2 (N odd) or (N|p) = +1."""
    fb: List[int] = []
    for p in primes_up_to(B):
        if p == 2:
            fb.append(2)
        elif N % p == 0 or legendre(N, p) == 1:
            fb.append(p)
    return fb


def log_sieve(N: int, a: int, M: int, fb: List[int], K: int) -> Tuple[List[float], int]:
    """Log sieve over x in [a, a+M): add log p at every hit of a line mod p^j, j <= K.
    Returns accumulators and the number of log-additions performed."""
    acc = [0.0] * M
    adds = 0
    for p in fb:
        lp = math.log(p)
        for j in range(1, K + 1):
            pj = p ** j
            if pj > (a + M) ** 2:
                break
            if p == 2:
                roots = [x for x in range(pj) if (x * x - N) % pj == 0]
            else:
                roots = hensel_roots(N, p, j)
            if not roots:
                break
            for r in roots:
                start = (r - a) % pj
                for i in range(start, M, pj):
                    acc[i] += lp
                    adds += 1
    return acc, adds


def section_sieve(N: int, B: int, M: int) -> List[Tuple[int, Dict[int, int]]]:
    print("=" * 72)
    print("3/4. Toy sieve over M = %d values above sqrt(N), B = %d" % (M, B))
    print("=" * 72)
    fb = admissible_factor_base(N, B)
    all_primes = primes_up_to(B)
    print("all primes <= B: %d     admissible (QR-restricted) primes: %d" % (len(all_primes), len(fb)))
    print("factor base:", fb)
    a = math.isqrt(N) + 1

    # Ground truth by trial division over ALL primes <= B (the naive method).
    divisions = 0
    truth: List[Tuple[int, Dict[int, int]]] = []
    for i in range(M):
        x = a + i
        v = x * x - N
        e, cof = {}, v
        for p in all_primes:
            divisions += 1
            while cof % p == 0:
                cof //= p
                divisions += 1
                e[p] = e.get(p, 0) + 1
        if cof == 1:
            truth.append((x, e))
    print("trial division: %d divisions (%.1f per value); smooth values: %d"
          % (divisions, divisions / M, len(truth)))
    # Every prime that ever appears is admissible: p | x^2 - N forces (N|p)=+1.
    used = {p for _, e in truth for p in e}
    assert used <= set(fb)
    print("primes actually used by relations are all admissible:", sorted(used))

    def run(K: int) -> Tuple[List[int], int]:
        acc, adds = log_sieve(N, a, M, fb, K)
        surv = [a + i for i in range(M)
                if abs(acc[i] - math.log((a + i) ** 2 - N)) < 1e-6]
        return surv, adds

    Kfull = int(math.log2((a + M) ** 2 - N)) + 1
    surv_full, adds_full = run(Kfull)
    surv_one, adds_one = run(1)
    truth_x = [x for x, _ in truth]
    sqf = [x for x, e in truth if all(c == 1 for c in e.values())]
    print("full sieve (K = %d): %d survivors, %d log-adds (%.2f per value)"
          % (Kfull, len(surv_full), adds_full, adds_full / M))
    print("  survivors == trial-division smooth set?", surv_full == truth_x)
    print("first-power sieve (K = 1): %d survivors" % len(surv_one))
    print("  survivors == squarefree smooth set?    ", surv_one == sqf)
    lost = 1 - len(surv_one) / max(1, len(truth_x))
    print("  fraction of relations lost by the first-power bug: %.1f%%" % (100 * lost))
    assert surv_full == truth_x and surv_one == sqf

    # Survivor-filter cost: additions + trial division of survivors only.
    surv_div = 0
    for x in surv_full:
        _, _ = factorize_small(x * x - N, fb)
        surv_div += len(fb)
    cost_sieve = adds_full + surv_div
    print("sieve cost = %d adds + %d survivor divisions = %d"
          % (adds_full, surv_div, cost_sieve))
    print("advantage (naive divisions / sieve operations) = %.2fx\n" % (divisions / cost_sieve))
    return truth


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Effective u
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
def dickman_rho(u: float, h: float = 1e-3) -> float:
    """Dickman rho by Euler integration of u rho'(u) = -rho(u-1)."""
    if u <= 1:
        return 1.0
    n1 = int(round(1 / h))
    vals = [1.0] * (n1 + 1)
    n = int(round(u / h))
    for i in range(n1 + 1, n + 1):
        t = i * h
        vals.append(vals[-1] - h * vals[i - n1 - 1] / t)
    return vals[n]


def section_effective_u() -> None:
    print("=" * 72)
    print("5. Effective u from the quadratic-residue restriction")
    print("=" * 72)
    print("    B       v        u     factor lnB/(lnB-ln2)   u_eff   rho(u_eff)/rho(u)")
    for B, v in [(60, 10 ** 7), (500, 10 ** 8), (2000, 10 ** 10), (10 ** 4, 10 ** 12)]:
        u = math.log(v) / math.log(B)
        f = math.log(B) / (math.log(B) - math.log(2))
        ueff = math.log(v) / math.log(B / 2)
        assert abs(ueff - u * f) < 1e-12 and ueff > u
        print("%6d  %8.0e  %6.3f   %10.4f            %6.3f   %6.3f"
              % (B, v, u, f, ueff, dickman_rho(ueff) / dickman_rho(u)))
    print("Identity ln v / ln(B/2) = u * lnB/(lnB - ln2) holds; the ratio < 1\n"
          "is the predicted yield shrinkage relative to the plain rho(u) model.\n")


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Linear algebra over GF(2) and the congruence of squares
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
def gf2_dependencies(vectors: List[int], n_rows: int) -> List[int]:
    """Gaussian elimination over GF(2).  vectors[i] is a bitmask of exponent
    parities.  Returns dependencies as bitmasks over relation indices."""
    pivots: Dict[int, Tuple[int, int]] = {}
    deps: List[int] = []
    for i, v in enumerate(vectors):
        comb = 1 << i
        for bit in range(n_rows - 1, -1, -1):
            if not (v >> bit) & 1:
                continue
            if bit in pivots:
                pv, pc = pivots[bit]
                v ^= pv
                comb ^= pc
            else:
                pivots[bit] = (v, comb)
                break
        if v == 0:
            deps.append(comb)
    return deps


def section_factor(N: int, relations: List[Tuple[int, Dict[int, int]]]) -> None:
    print("=" * 72)
    print("6. From relations to a factor")
    print("=" * 72)
    # (a) The certificate quoted in the paper.
    cert = [10248, 10342, 10749, 18185]
    vals = [x * x - N for x in cert]
    prod_v = math.prod(vals)
    Y = math.isqrt(prod_v)
    X = math.prod(cert)
    assert Y * Y == prod_v
    print("certificate abscissae:", cert)
    for x, v in zip(cert, vals):
        print("  %5d^2 - N = %9d = %s" % (x, v, factorize_small(v, primes_up_to(60))[0]))
    print("product of values = Y^2 with Y =", Y)
    print("X = prod x_i =", X, ";  N | X^2 - Y^2 ?", (X * X - Y * Y) % N == 0)
    g = math.gcd(X - Y, N)
    print("gcd(X - Y, N) =", g, "  N / g =", N // g)
    assert g == 9127 and N // g == 11369
    tri = [10342, 10749, 18185]
    Xt = math.prod(tri)
    Yt = math.isqrt(math.prod(x * x - N for x in tri))
    print("3-relation dependency: Y =", Yt, " (X - Y) mod N =", (Xt - Yt) % N, "-> trivial")

    # (b) Live: GF(2) elimination on the relations collected in section 3.
    fb = sorted({p for _, e in relations for p in e})
    idx = {p: j for j, p in enumerate(fb)}
    vecs = []
    for _, e in relations:
        m = 0
        for p, c in e.items():
            if c % 2:
                m |= 1 << idx[p]
        vecs.append(m)
    deps = gf2_dependencies(vecs, len(fb))
    print("\nlive run: %d relations over %d primes -> %d dependencies"
          % (len(relations), len(fb), len(deps)))
    useful = 0
    for d in deps:
        xs = [relations[i][0] for i in range(len(relations)) if (d >> i) & 1]
        Xd = math.prod(xs) % N
        Yd = math.isqrt(math.prod(x * x - N for x in xs)) % N
        g = math.gcd(Xd - Yd, N)
        if 1 < g < N:
            useful += 1
    if deps:
        print("dependencies giving a proper factor: %d / %d  (CRT predicts ~1/2)"
              % (useful, len(deps)))

    # (c) The CRT coin flip: four square roots, two useful.
    p, q = 9127, 11369
    y = 123456 % N
    s = (y * y) % N
    roots_p = [y % p, (-y) % p]
    roots_q = [y % q, (-y) % q]
    roots = sorted({(a * q * pow(q, -1, p) + b * p * pow(p, -1, q)) % N
                    for a in roots_p for b in roots_q})
    print("\nsquare roots of y^2 mod N for y = %d:" % y)
    for r in roots:
        tag = "trivial (+-y)" if r in (y, (-y) % N) else "useful: gcd = %d" % math.gcd(r - y, N)
        assert r * r % N == s
        print("  %9d   %s" % (r, tag))
    assert len(roots) == 4


def main() -> None:
    section_hensel(N_TOY)
    section_two_adic(N_TOY)
    rels = section_sieve(N_TOY, B=60, M=60000)
    section_effective_u()
    section_factor(N_TOY, rels)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
